create_nuclearindustry.ponder.accelerato: Building a Linac
A particle accelerator starts at its controller. The beam leaves it on the face opposite its panel.
Right in front of it goes the Ion Source, with its shaft across the beam. It turns hydrogen into protons: fill it by pipe.
From the source the beamline runs on. Each RF Cavity adds energy: a longer linac with more cavities reaches higher energies.
Quadrupole Magnets keep the beam focused. Put one at least every four blocks, or most of the beam is lost on the walls.
The line ends in a Beam Dump or a target. The dump soaks up the whole beam, and becomes radioactive doing it.
Klystrons, Magnet Power Supplies and Vacuum Pumps beside the line power it, from a shaft or with Forge Energy.
Right-click the controller to open its panel and start the beam. It glows through the windows of the Beam Pipes.
Building a Synchrotron
A synchrotron ring takes the beam round and round, gaining energy on every turn. The injector line ends in an Injection Septum facing the ring's centre.
Sneak-right-click it, or open a door beside it, and the interlock opens and the beam trips. While the beam runs, the doors beside a panel stay locked.
Right-click the controller and start the beam: it is injected, ramped up round the ring and extracted into the station.
The ring is a circle of radius 6 or more, one block high, and every block of it must be a ring element. Ring Dipole Magnets bend the beam round it.
Put a Quadrupole Magnet in every sector of about eight blocks to keep the beam focused, and RF cavities to speed it up on each turn.
Superconducting Ring Dipoles and Superconducting RF Cavities are stronger but need liquid helium: an Accelerator Cryo Feed beside the ring takes it in by pipe and gives the warm gas back.
Klystrons, Magnet Power Supplies and Vacuum Pumps serve the ring from beside it, as on a linac.
Exactly one Extraction Septum lets the beam out of the ring, facing the way it leaves.
The extraction line ends in a Target Station with its window towards the beam. It soaks up the beam like a dump...
...and above 25 GeV its horn collects antiprotons and pushes them into a Penning trap or an Antimatter Conduit beside it. Power the trap before the first antiproton arrives!
Beam Interlock panels keep people out of the ring. The beam only runs while every interlock beside it is secured: right-click one to search and secure it.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.antimatter: Antimatter Containment
Antimatter is kept in Penning traps: a magnetic field between two magnet heads holds a cloud of antiprotons away from the glass. Each size has its own colour.
Putting antimatter into an unpowered trap, or breaking a loaded one, annihilates it at once. The blast breaks the traps beside it, and they go off in turn: keep them apart!
The Small Penning Trap holds 32 ng, the Penning Trap, two blocks tall, 256 ng, and the Large Penning Trap, 2x2 and three high, 2048 ng.
Every trap needs Forge Energy all the time, more the fuller it is. A Creative RF Generator gives what its value board says; in survival, bring FE by cable.
The light on the front tells how the field is doing: green when stable, amber when its buffer runs low.
Right-click a powered trap with an Antimatter Vial to put it in the port. The wrench switches the port between filling the vial and emptying it into the trap.
A loaded vial's battery holds its field for thirty seconds away from a powered port. When it runs out, the vial annihilates wherever it is.
An Antimatter Conduit moves antimatter between the traps it joins. Every block of it needs a little FE; without it, nothing moves.
If a loaded trap loses its power, its buffer lasts about ten seconds. Then it quenches: red lights, sparks and an alarm for three seconds...
...and the antimatter annihilates: a blast that grows with the charge, a flash and a pulse of gamma rays. It leaves no fallout.
Antimatter Engine
The strongest engine there is. The controller is an annihilation chamber; behind it, magnetic coils and a magnetic nozzle.
Feed it antimatter with a conduit or a vial in its port, and Forge Energy for the coils' field.
More coils turn more of the annihilation into thrust. What they miss heats them, and too few at full throttle wear through.
The gamma rays they miss stream out behind the nozzle: keep out of the jet.
Without energy the field fails: a quench alarm sounds, and the chamber's antimatter annihilates where the engine is.
Annihilation Generator
The Annihilation Generator burns antiprotons in a small chamber of its own, 1 ng, behind the porthole on its back.
It draws antimatter from a Penning trap or an Antimatter Conduit beside it, or from a vial put in the socket on its top.
To start, its chamber needs FE for its field: without it the generator takes no antimatter in, and a loaded vial in its socket runs its battery flat.
A redstone signal sets the throttle. With no signal it keeps a small standby burn that holds its own field, and the mode lamp blinks.
The panel on top, or the wrench on that face, picks the mode. Rotation turns the shaft at 256 RPM with a great deal of stress capacity...
...Electric pushes FE out of its terminals into every block beside it, and Split gives half of each.
In Electric or Split mode it powers the trap that feeds it and its own chamber: once running, it no longer needs any other source.
The core glows brighter the harder it burns and flickers when the supply cannot keep up. A comparator reads its output.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.antiproton: The Antiproton Injector is a block of a tokamak's shell. Its port faces out; its nozzle looks into the plasma.
It needs FE and antimatter: from a trap or a conduit beside it, or a vial in its port. Its little chamber holds four doses.
The wrench sets it to fire on its own, only with a redstone signal, or never. The amber lamp shows it armed.
The green lamp means it is ready: armed, powered and loaded with a dose. Only the plasma is missing.
While the tokamak heats, once its plasma is well confined and dense enough, the injector fires one dose of antiprotons into it...
...and their annihilation ignites the plasma at once, without heating it all the way. Then the injector cools down for ten seconds.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.centrifuge: The Centrifuge separates uranium hexafluoride by enrichment. It turns through its back, at 32 RPM or more.
Pipe UF6 into the top or the sides.
The enriched product leaves through the front...
...and the depleted tails through the bottom.
Chain centrifuges into a cascade: natural to LEU, LEU to HEU, HEU to weapons grade. Pipe each stage's tails back into the stage before it.
It also separates Lithium-6 from lithium.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.civil_defe: Blast Doors
A blast door is a rectangle of steel or lead Blast Door leaves, 2x2 to 4x4, with a ring of Blast Door Frame around it.
One block of the ring is the Blast Door Controller. Its shaft runs through the wall, across the door.
A rising redstone signal opens it: the panel slides sideways into the wall, towards the controller...
...and a falling one shuts it. A shaft turning one way opens it and the other way shuts it, faster the faster it turns.
Shut, it holds back blast waves and radiation; open, the doorway lets both through. A comparator reads how far open it is.
If a leaf or a frame block is broken, the door slams shut.
Fallout Shelters
A Shelter Filtration Unit certifies the sealed room it stands in as a shelter.
Every wall block the air touches must hold back blasts and radiation well enough: glass will not do. Goggles on the unit name the weakest wall.
Inside a certified shelter a blast wave keeps only a tenth of its force. A shut blast door counts as wall.
While the unit turns at 16 RPM or more it filters the air: fallout and contaminated ground give those inside a twentieth of their dose.
A Seismic Detector feels every nuclear detonation in its dimension. Goggles show the distance, bearing and strength of the last eight.
A comparator reads it: the signal jumps with a blast and fades back to 0 over five minutes.
Sirens
The Air Raid Siren sounds a steady alert while it gets a redstone signal.
Bomb countdowns and plant accidents trigger automatic warnings. Missile alerts require a powered radar connected by redstone.
Goggles on it tell how long until the impact. It is heard up to 128 blocks away.
The Hand-Crank Siren has no power of its own: it sounds while the shaft under it turns at 32 RPM or more...
...and wails higher the faster it turns. A comparator reads 15 from it while it sounds.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.containmen: A Containment Door is the way into a containment. Shut, it seals like the wall around it and holds 8 bar.
Click it or give it a redstone signal: it pulls out of its frame and slides sideways along the wall.
Open, the doorway is a hole: the containment is no longer sealed until the door shuts again.
While the containment behind it is more than 0.2 bar above the outside, the door is pressure-locked: neither a click nor redstone opens it.
Two doors side by side, hinged on opposite sides, open together and slide apart.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.control_ro: The Control Room
A control room runs a whole plant from one place. This one is laid out like a real plant's: tall instrument boards on the back wall, and the operators' desks set back in front of them.
Control Tables have a flat top, level with a desk's rail: here, the shift supervisor's at the back. Tables apart from the desks make a console of their own.
Look at a module or a console to see its card on the right of the screen: what it is set to, what it shows, where its redstone goes and what the console is linked to.
Every device starts unlinked. Click any block of a machine with the Control Room Linker, then click the device: reactors, steam generators, containments, turbines, cooling towers and tokamaks.
Linked to any other block, a device watches the radiation there. Devices reach 128 blocks; sneak-click one with the linker to unlink it.
Desks, tables and wall panels touching side by side, and wall panels above one another, make one console with one link: link any block of it and the whole console follows.
So the whole back board is one console on the reactor. Wall Control Panels hang on the face of a solid block and hold four modules upright.
Monitors side by side join into one screen of up to 8x8. A big screen lists the machine's readings beside a two-minute graph; a lone monitor shows one big reading per page.
Click a screen to change page, and wrench it to choose its title, layout, style, rows and up to three graph lines. A comparator reads its main value.
Control Desks join side by side and turn corners like stairs, so a console can wrap round its operators. A corner desk holds one module on each arm.
Consoles on different walls are separate: this one runs the tokamak. Each monitor screen links on its own, here to the tokamak and to a turbine, each in a style of its own.
Instruments and Screens
LED Displays show a reading in digits with its unit. In a row they join into one wider display of up to eight modules, set up by the leftmost: the wider, the more digits, with a label on top.
Chart Recorders draw up to three readings on paper. Feed them paper by hand or with a hopper, and wrench them to choose the pens and the speed.
Sneak-click one with an empty hand to tear the chart off as a Chart Roll, to read anywhere. A comparator reads the paper left.
Nuclear Alarms ring and power every side once their reading passes the threshold. Pick the reading on the top face and the threshold on the sides.
Too big a value reads OL; a reading the machine does not have reads dashes.
Bar Graphs show a reading as a column of twenty lights: green, amber in the 15%% under the alarm level and red from it. The alarm level is set in the module's screen.
Trend Recorders draw a reading over their last 48 samples, one every 1, 5 or 20 seconds.
The Core Map shows a fission core from above, north at the top: fuel green to red as it burns, control channels filling blue as their rods go in. Four in one block make one big map.
The Plasma Section is a cut through a tokamak: its plasma glows with the temperature, swells with the density and shakes as it grows unstable. Four in one block make one big screen too.

Annunciator Panels hang on the wall, six alarm windows each, and side by side make one board. Link a window with the linker, or the plate for all six; wrench it to set its alarm, threshold, severity and label.

A tripped window flashes and the horn sounds until ACK; it stays lit while the alarm lasts, flashes slowly once clear and goes dark on RESET. Alarms are red, warnings amber; the board rings the first to trip.

The board's buttons sit at the right of its bottom strip: TEST lights every lamp, SIL quiets the horn, then ACK and RESET. Redstone presses them: left ACK, right RESET, above SIL, below TEST. A waiting alarm powers the wall.
Control Modules
Fit a control module by clicking a free slot with it. Straight desks, tables and wall panels hold four; a corner desk holds one on each arm.
Its lamp is green while it drives. Click it to raise the setpoint and sneak-click to lower it; its setup switches it to standby.
Indicator Lamps light on SCRAM, running, no signal, an open relief valve or any alarm. Gauges show one reading on a dial.
Wrench a module to set it up: its function, label, reading or alarm, and its redstone output. Functions the linked machine cannot use are greyed out.
Sneak-wrench a module to take just that module out. Sneak-wrench the block anywhere else to pick it up; its modules drop beside it.
Click a module with an empty hand to work it. The Push Button SCRAMs the reactor or resets the SCRAM, sends a pulse, or starts and shuts down a tokamak.
The Guarded Button keeps a SCRAM or a shutdown under a hinged cover: the first click lifts the cover, the second presses the button.
A sneaking click lets the cover down, and it falls shut by itself five seconds after the last click.
Levers switch the automatic SCRAM, the pressurizer heaters and spray, a tokamak's fuel, heating, start or shutdown, or a plain signal. The Key Switch turns a signal on and off.
Dials set the control rods' target, the automatic SCRAM threshold or a redstone level: click to turn one up, sneak-click to turn it down.
The Controller is an automatic operator: it holds reactor power or temperature through the rod target, primary pressure through the pressurizer, or a tokamak's fusion power.
Signals Out of the Room
Any module can put its state out as redstone, chosen in its setup: a lever or a lamp on or off, a button's pulse, a dial's level or a reading from 0 to 15.
Below the desk: out of the bottom and the back of the block it sits in.
On a Create Redstone Link frequency: pick its two items in the setup, and every receiver on that frequency within range puts the signal out.
Or on an Advanced Redstone Link code: four letters or digits instead of two items. Click the link to type its code; sneak-click it to switch between sending and receiving.

create_nuclearindustry.ponder.fuel_cycle: Uranium goes from the ground to a reactor in a line of Create machines. First, Crushing Wheels grind Raw Uranium into Crushed Raw Uranium.

create_nuclearindustry.ponder.isotopes.t: Cobalt-60 is made in a fission reactor: build a Reactor Irradiation Channel into its wall in place of a casing block.

create_nuclearindustry.ponder.launch_bas: Start with a 3×3 square of Launch Base blocks. It is the complete launch site floor; Silo Concrete walls are optional decoration.

create_nuclearindustry.ponder.maintenanc: A plant's parts wear with use: the reactor's control rod drives and relief valve, a steam generator's tubes, a turbine's blades. Worn out, they fail.

create_nuclearindustry.ponder.missile_ra: Turn the radar at 32 RPM or more. It sees a rocket body about 3 km away, further when it turns faster and much further while a booster burns. Its dish turns with the sweep.

create_nuclearindustry.ponder.nuclear_th: A rocket for Create Aeronautics ships, heated by a reactor. Build it in a line: the controller, heat exchanger segments along the engine, and a nozzle facing the way the exhaust leaves.
Pipe hot primary coolant from a pressurized reactor and a propellant into the controller, and take the cooled primary back from it.
Water, deuterium or hydrogen: the lighter the gas, the harder it pushes. Each segment passes more propellant.
A redstone signal sets the throttle. Aboard a ship it pushes the ship opposite to its nozzle.

create_nuclearindustry.ponder.plant_cont: The control room runs the plant from afar. Fit control modules into Control Desks and link them to the reactor with the Control Room Linker.
Containment Penetrations carry the pipes through the wall without unsealing it.
The weakest wall sets the limit: this window holds only 1.05 bar. If the pressure beats it, the wall bursts there and everything airborne escapes.
A Containment Monitor inside measures the sealed air: pressure, temperature, steam, hydrogen and airborne activity.
Overheated cladding gives off hydrogen. Above 4%% it may burn and above 8%% it always does: Recombiners remove it without a flame.
A Filtered Vent opened by redstone bleeds off the overpressure and lets out only 1%% of the airborne activity.
In a meltdown the fuel turns into Corium, which melts its way down...
...until a Core Catcher floor stops it: it spreads out and freezes into Solidified Corium, still radioactive but contained.
A dial set to Rod target chooses how deep the control rods should sit.

...so wire them to a Clutch and a Gearshift on the piston's shaft: the rods move while a port is lit, the way it asks.

create_nuclearindustry.ponder.plant_gene: The secondary loop turns the reactor's heat into rotation. It starts at the steam generator, heated by the primary loop.

...where every rotor stage expands it and the Turbine Output turns the shaft.

This tower, radius 4 and 12 high, condenses 24 mB/t. If the exhaust backs up the turbine stops, so size the tower for its turbines.
The water leaves through a port set to OUTPUT, and a pump sends it back to the steam generator's feedwater port.

Steam left in the generator raises its pressure until it stops taking heat, so the turbine must keep drawing it.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.plant_heat: A pressurized water reactor keeps its coolant liquid under pressure. Fill a fission reactor with Primary Coolant: water and boron from a mixer.
...and the cold leg brings it back, cooled, to the reactor. The flow is whatever the pumps move, and a pressurized core needs plenty.
In the tubes its heat boils the feedwater on the other side into steam. The two never mix.
If a pump stops, the core heats up and boils, the pressure climbs and the relief valve lifts.
A broken pipe drains the loop until the core uncovers and overheats. Primary coolant is radioactive: a leak irradiates.
Stand a Pressurizer on the lid, away from the controller and the rod channels: 2 to 4 Pressurizer or Heater Port blocks under a Relief Valve.
Its steam bubble holds the loop at 155 bar. Heater Ports raise the pressure, on their own or by redstone after a wrench click; spray from the cold leg lowers it.
The Relief Valve lifts at 170 bar and reseats at 160. It can stick open: a redstone signal on it shuts its block valve.
A port set to OUTPUT is the hot leg, one set to INPUT the cold leg. Without a pressurizer they refuse primary coolant.
The Steam Generator is a 3x3 column, 4 to 8 high, of casing around a core of Tube Bundles. More tubes carry more heat.
Its controller goes in a side wall, facing out, with a Tube Bundle right behind it.
Each Steam Generator Port carries one thing, picked with the wrench: primary in, primary out, feedwater in or steam out.
Create pumps drive the loop. The hot leg carries the hot primary coolant from the reactor to the primary inlet...
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.plant_loss: The worst case is losing the cooling. Feed pumps turned by the plant's own turbine stop with it at a SCRAM, and the decay heat stays.
With nothing feeding it, the water boils away and the core uncovers.
Above 1200 °C the zirconium cladding reacts with the steam and gives off hydrogen.
Without a containment, the hydrogen gathers in any closed room around the reactor. From 4%% it may ignite...
...and from 8%% it always does, blowing the roof off: an INES incident with sirens, as at Fukushima. In open air it disperses.
A sealed containment keeps the hydrogen in, and Recombiners set in its walls remove it before it burns.
Water bled from a damaged core comes out as Contaminated Water: treat it as low-level waste.
Give the feed pumps a drive of their own, apart from the turbine, and a SCRAM ends in a cold shutdown instead.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.plant_over: A nuclear power plant is a chain of machines joined by pipes and shafts. Here it is whole: each step zooms in on one part and how it joins the next.
The control room runs it all from a distance: link its desks, annunciator and chart recorder to the reactor with the Control Room Linker.
Spent fuel taken out of the reactor goes into the racks at the bottom of the pool, under water, with a Pool Cooler to carry off its heat.
Once it has cooled, move it to Dry Storage Casks or send it to reprocessing.
That is the whole plant, running. The next scenes explain each part in detail.
The reactor and its steam generator stand inside the containment, a sealed room of Containment Concrete with a Containment Door to walk in. From here on it is shown cut away.
In the primary loop a pump carries the hot Primary Coolant from the reactor's OUTPUT port to the steam generator's primary in...
...and a second pump brings it back from primary out to the reactor's INPUT port. The Pressurizer on the lid keeps the loop under pressure.
Pipes may only leave the containment through Containment Penetrations: one for the steam line, one for the feedwater.
The steam line runs from the Steam Out port on top of the steam generator, through its penetration and a pump, into the turbine's INPUT port.
The Turbine Output turns the shaft at the turbine's end: take the rotation from there to your machines.
The turbine's Exhaust Port sends the spent steam, through another pump, to the Cooling Tower's INPUT port.
The tower condenses it into water. From its OUTPUT port a pump sends the water through the other penetration to the steam generator's feedwater port: the loop is closed.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.plant_safe: A SCRAM stops the chain reaction, not the heat: the fuel keeps making decay heat, a few percent of its power, long after.
Rods first: with as many inserted control rod blocks as fuel rod blocks, any core stays subcritical even when cold.
Fewer rods than that? Pump in Boric Acid, mixed from water, borax salt and sulfuric acid. Its boron holds the core down from the water.
Boiling never takes the water below 100 °C. Feed cold water through an input port, with a pump that has a drive of its own...
...and, once the chain reaction is off, bleed the hot water out of an output port. It never bleeds the core dry.
Send the Hot Water to a Cooling Tower, never straight back in: it returns as water. Bleeding also washes the boron out, to dilute it for a restart.
Goggles on the reactor show the way down: Subcritical, Hot shutdown, then Cold shutdown, held with margin under 100 °C and the core under water.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.plant_wast: Fuel leaves the reactor as Hot spent fuel, dated with the day it came out. It goes under water first.
Packages end up in a geological repository, where each one is scored. Depth below the surface counts most: full marks 64 blocks down.
Then the host rock around it, such as deepslate, tuff or basalt, and the waste form: vitrified is best, a raw barrel worst.
Backfill every face with Bentonite, made from clay and borax, or with other packages.
Water within 4 blocks spoils the site: water is what carries waste out.
From a score of 80%% a package is stored: it neither leaks nor irradiates. A Repository Inspector shows the weakest package within 8 blocks.
A Spent Fuel Rack holds nine assemblies on the floor of a pool. Each block of water above cuts its radiation: two stop over 97%%.
Spent fuel cools with time: Warm after about 2 days, Cooled after a week and Aged after 3 weeks. Fresh fuel glows blue.
Its decay heat warms the pool, and a pool too small for its racks boils dry. A Pool Cooler turned from above carries the heat away.
Once Warm or cooler, fuel can move to a Dry Storage Cask. It lets out only 2%% of the radiation and never leaks.
Or reprocess it (PUREX): crush it, dissolve it in nitric acid and centrifuge the solution for uranium and plutonium. Cooled fuel yields more and leaves less waste.
Waste comes in three classes. Low-Level Waste, from scrubbers and contaminated water, is compacted with an iron sheet into a Compacted Waste Drum.
Intermediate-Level Waste is cemented in a mixer, with sand, gravel, an iron sheet and water, into a Cemented Waste Drum.
High-Level Waste from PUREX melts with sand and borax into a Vitrified Waste Canister, in a Vitrification Melter on a lit Blaze Burner.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.radiation_: Fallout leaves the ground contaminated: green dust rises from it, and standing on it irradiates.
A Radiation Scrubber draws it out of the ground of its chunk and the eight around it, the worst first. Drive it from below: it cleans faster up to 256 RPM.
What it absorbs comes out as Low-Level Waste, for a Compacted Waste Drum. Take it out with a funnel or hopper: full, it stops, and the waste inside irradiates.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.reactor_co: The reactor is a multiblock: raise a hollow shell of Reactor Casing.

Right-click the controller to form the reactor.
A Mechanical Piston above an open channel raises and lowers the Control Rods.
Super Glue the rods to each other and to the piston head so they move as one.
Withdrawn rods absorb fewer neutrons: the power rises until the hotter fuel and water hold it at a new level.
Inserted rods soak up neutrons: the deeper they sit, the more the reaction is throttled. Fully inserted means shutdown.
The width must be odd (3-9) and the height 4-12.
Inside, raise columns of Fuel Channels: each block holds one fuel assembly.
A central column of Heat Exchangers carries the heat into the coolant.
Control Rods on the corners absorb neutrons: they are the reactor's brakes.
Swap wall casing for a Reactor Fluid Port set to INPUT for coolant...
...and another set to OUTPUT for steam.
A Reactor Fuel Port loads fuel assemblies and ejects spent fuel.
Cap the reactor and place the Reactor Controller at the centre of the top face.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.reactor_mo: Graphite Moderator fills whole interior columns. It slows neutrons, so the Fuel Channels sharing a face with it split more often.
A fuel column with two graphite neighbours is fully moderated; one with a single neighbour, half. A fully moderated core is 35%% more reactive.
Beryllium Reflector belongs in the columns that touch the shell: it bounces escaping neutrons back into the core.
A ring lined all round adds reactivity too. Both make the same fuel more reactive, so leave room for enough Control Rods.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.reactor_re: A Reactor Redstone Port takes the place of a casing block in the shell and puts out a 0-15 signal on its panel side.

Control Rods only move with pistons. Carry the signal to whatever drives them, here a Redstone Link pair and a Gearshift on the piston's shaft.
On SCRAM the Gearshift reverses the piston and the rods go all the way in. Without such wiring, SCRAM only lights the port.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.rtg.text_1: A Radioisotope Generator turns the decay heat of a pellet into a steady 16 RPM on its front shaft. Right-click with a pellet, or feed it by hopper.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.rtg.text_2: Plutonium pellets give 256 stress capacity per RPM and lose half of it every 10 in-game days; waste pellets give 64 and halve every 2. Below a quarter they come out spent.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.rtg.text_3: It irradiates whoever stands near it...
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.rtg.text_4: ...so wall it in. A Block of Depleted Uranium lets only a tenth of the radiation through.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.servo_gear: The Servo Gearbox puts a Mechanical Piston or a Rope Pulley where a redstone signal says. Either end of its shaft takes the rotation; the other end drives.
It finds the actuator through shafts, gearboxes and cogs, and moves it a share of its stroke: no signal keeps it in, a full signal runs it all the way.
Scroll the top or bottom to set the stroke in blocks. It is cut to how far the actuator reaches: a piston's poles, a pulley's rope.
A weaker signal, a shorter move: 8 of 15 of a 3-block stroke is 1.6, so 2 blocks. It always stops on a whole block.
Scroll the other two sides to choose whether a stronger signal extends or retracts.
It stops the actuator exactly on the block and lets it set its blocks down. Every actuator turned at the same speed moves alike; if something blocks the way, it waits and tries again.
A comparator reads where the actuator stands, on the same scale as the signal.
Send it the redstone of a Control Desk dial set to Control rod target, and the rods follow the desk without clutch or gearshift.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.silo_launc: Supply at least 32 RPM to the Launch Controller. Its default stress impact is 8 SU per RPM. Load the warhead in its console, then arm the prepared rocket on the Launch tab.

The rocket lifts off whole and drops its spent stages as falling debris. Missiles warn no one by themselves: radars do.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.tag.contro: Everything to watch and run a plant from one room: screens, consoles, modules, annunciators, recorders and alarms
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.tag.nuclea: Everything a nuclear power plant is made of: the reactor and its loops, the turbine hall, the control room, the containment and the spent fuel
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.tokamak.te: A tokamak holds a ring of plasma with magnets. Start with a Central Solenoid column, five blocks tall, at its axis.
Keep the coolant flowing. A tokamak without coolant overheats and disrupts, blowing holes in its vessel.
The torus has a 5x5 cross-section. Its floor and roof can hold Breeding Blankets, which turn fusion neutrons into tritium.
Toroidal Field Coils line the walls. The 3x3 core of the ring must stay empty: it is the plasma chamber.
The ring may be 4 to 16 blocks from the solenoid to the plasma. A bigger ring holds more plasma and makes more power.
The Tokamak Controller sits on the outer equator. Right-click it to form the tokamak and open its control panel.
A Fluid Port on INPUT takes water as coolant...
...and one on OUTPUT gives plasma steam for a Plasma Turbine.
The Fuel Injector takes deuterium and tritium, by pipe or by hand with gas cells. On deuterium alone the plasma runs slowly and breeds its first tritium.
Magnet Drives turn rotation into the confining field: one for every 4 blocks of radius, at 64 RPM or more.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.tokamak_st: A tokamak does not start by itself. Before its plasma can burn it needs a vacuum, cold magnets, a field and heating.
Burning, a dense and well confined plasma can ignite: turn the heating down and it keeps itself hot.
Vacuum Pumps in the shell empty the plasma chamber: one for every 4 blocks of radius, turning at 128 RPM.
Cryogenic Ports feed the coils liquid helium from a Cryogenic Plant: INPUT takes it in, OUTPUT sends the boiled-off helium back.
Superconducting coils must stay below 20 K. If the helium runs out they warm up and the tokamak shuts down safely.
Neutral Beam Injectors and RF Antennas heat the plasma. Antennas only couple to a dense enough plasma; beams burn a little deuterium.
Heating takes a lot of rotation. Fusion gives back Q times the heating: below a Q of about 3 the plant spends more than it makes.
Press Start in the controller's screen, give it a redstone pulse or throw a desk lever. The screen shows each phase and what is missing.
It pumps down, cools the coils and ramps up the field; then a solenoid pulse breaks a puff of deuterium down into plasma.
Viewports let you watch it: the plasma glows from red to white as it heats, and the windows light up the hall.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.turbine.te: A turbine is a box of casing: 3 to 7 blocks wide and high, and 3 to 16 blocks long.
A column of rotors runs down its axis. Every rotor stage expands 40 mB/t of steam.
Reinforced Turbine Glass can replace casing anywhere on a face, but not on edges or corners.
Fluid Ports go on the faces. One set to INPUT takes the steam...
...and one set to OUTPUT returns the condensed water. Each pair passes 160 mB/t.

create_nuclearindustry.ponder.waste_stor: At the surface a Waste Barrel irradiates whoever comes close, and slowly leaks into the ground around it.
Underground, a repository score decides: depth below the surface, host rock such as deepslate around it, Bentonite backfill on its faces and the waste form. Water within 4 blocks spoils it.

From a score of 80%% a package neither irradiates nor leaks. Raw barrels score lowest: bury them deep in host rock, pack them in Bentonite, or treat the waste first. The old Y=0 rule is a config option.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.waste_tran: Radioactive Waste Cisterns connect like Create's fluid tanks: up to 3x3 across, 8 buckets a block.
Fill them with pipes. They take only radioactive fluids: spent fuel solution, nitrates, contaminated water...
Anything else is refused, so nothing else can be pumped in, not even into a moving train.
Shielded Waste Casks join along their axis like Item Vaults. They hold solid waste, packages and cooled spent fuel; Hot fuel is refused.
Sealed, their shell lets almost no radiation out. Both ride Create trains, where Portable Storage Interfaces and schedule conditions see the cargo.

Two uses of a Maintenance Kit, by hand or from a Deployer, patch the breach.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.weapons_bo: The Nuclear Bomb takes weapons-grade cores in its three slots, two to a slot: each is eight uranium at 90%% or more, or four plutonium.
The more cores it holds, the further it wrecks: six reach 250 blocks out, round a crater a third as wide.
Power it with redstone: after a ten second countdown it goes off. Sirens in reach sound the attack warning meanwhile.
Its flash burns whoever sees it, a blast wave rolls outwards throwing whoever stands in the open, and fallout drifts downwind.
The Dirty Bomb takes anything radioactive that is not weapons-grade: waste, spent fuel, fragments, RTG pellets.
Its blast is small and leaves no crater, but it scatters its load as fallout, wider the more radioactive the load.
create_nuclearindustry.ponder.weapons_mi: A 3×3 Launch Base is all a rocket needs. Put the Launch Controller beside any side; a Silo Concrete shell is optional, and only changes the look.

The guidance sets the accuracy: empty it is basic, with a Precision Mechanism inertial, with a Star Tracker stellar. The controller shows the expected miss.

create_nuclearindustry.ponder.weapons_th: The Thermonuclear Bomb is a fission primary that lights a fusion secondary. Its first slot takes one weapons-grade core, the primary: without it, the bomb cannot go off.

Up to four Depleted Uranium Blocks make its tamper: a bigger blast, and far more fallout, with a hot spot that lasts for days.
Power it with redstone: after a fifteen second countdown it wrecks what stands up to 750 blocks away, three times an atomic bomb.
Its fireball burns bigger, whiter and longer, and the cloud it raises is near-black soot.
